meta.location: The temple in the land Bountiful
meta.unit: The law fulfilled and the other sheep (3 Nephi 15–16)
principles: A third flock he has not yet visited
A record written for readers centuries away
A blessing on the Gentiles and a warning attached to it

world_behind.title: The audience is still the twelve
world_behind.text: 3 Nephi 15:11 turned to them and this chapter continues without a break.

world_behind.title: A third group is named
world_behind.text: Verse 1 sets them outside this land, outside Jerusalem, and outside anywhere he has gone to minister. 3 Nephi 15:20 has already separated the other tribes from those at Jerusalem, so the record is now tracking three peoples who do not know of each other.

world_behind.title: The errand comes with its authority attached
world_behind.text: Verse 3 has the Father commanding him to go, and 3 Nephi 15:16 to 18 has already recorded what he was and was not commanded to say at Jerusalem. Each errand in these chapters is reported with the instruction behind it rather than as his own initiative.

world_behind.title: The record is commissioned in advance
world_behind.text: Verse 4 puts the writing after his departure and gives the reason for it. 3 Nephi 26:11 later reports that Mormon was forbidden to write the greater part of what was taught, so the commission and the restriction both belong to the same visit.

world_behind.title: The Father is quoted throughout
world_behind.text: Verses 7 to 14 keep saying "saith the Father" while Christ delivers the words, which makes the passage a quotation inside a quotation inside Mormon's abridgment.

world_behind.title: The Gentile conditions are stated three times in this visit
world_behind.text: The repentance-or-else terms at verses 13 and 15 are given again at 3 Nephi 20:15 to 20 and at 3 Nephi 21:14 to 22, to the same audience and in nearly the same words.

world_behind.title: The chapter closes in Isaiah, and returns there
world_behind.text: Verses 18 to 20 quote Isaiah 52:8 to 10 with almost no change, and 3 Nephi 20:32 to 35 quotes those same three verses again four chapters later.

words.text: Flock animals, and the people a shepherd keeps. The record uses the word twenty-six times, twice in this chapter, and the King James Bible one hundred and eighty-eight. Verse 1 makes it the name for people he has not yet visited.
One who keeps a flock. Treated at Helaman 15:13. It appears twenty-one times in the record, and the King James Bible forty-five, including John 10:16.

The nations outside Israel. Its count runs to one hundred and forty-one here, nine of those inside this chapter, against one hundred and twenty-nine in the King James Bible. Verse 4 puts them on the path the writing will travel.

Walked on, crushed underfoot. The word turns up fifteen times, twice inside this chapter, here, and the King James Bible twenty-seven. Verse 8 has Israel trodden by the Gentiles and verse 15 turns the direction around.
A name people repeat as an insult. The record uses the word twice, here and at 1 Nephi 19:14, and the King James Bible six times. Verse 9 pairs it with a hiss.

Sexual sin, and in the prophets the worship of other gods. Its count is twenty-seven times in this book, while the King James Bible thirty-two. Verse 10 lists it among the sins that end the fulness among the Gentiles.
Men posted to keep watch over a city. The record uses the word four times and the King James Bible twelve. Verse 18 is Isaiah 52:8 quoted whole.

phrases.term: Other sheep, which are not of this land, neither of the land of Jerusalem
phrases.text: A third flock, defined by where they are not. 3 Nephi 15:21 had just told these hearers they were the other sheep of John 10:16.

phrases.term: They who have not as yet heard my voice
phrases.text: The mark that separates this group from the one he is speaking to. 3 Nephi 15:24 had said these had both heard his voice and seen him.

phrases.term: That there may be one fold and one shepherd
phrases.text: The purpose given for the visit. The same clause closed the quotation in 3 Nephi 15:17 and 15:21.

phrases.term: I command you that ye shall write these sayings after I am gone
phrases.text: The writing is commanded on the spot. Verse 4 gives the chain the writing will pass through before it reaches anyone.

phrases.term: Through the fulness of the Gentiles, the remnant of their seed... may be brought in
phrases.text: The route home. Gentile hands carry the record to the descendants of the people hearing him.

phrases.term: Then will I fulfil the covenant which the Father hath made unto all the people of the house of Israel
phrases.text: The gathering and the covenant tied together. 3 Nephi 15:8 had said the covenant was not all fulfilled.

phrases.term: Blessed are the Gentiles, because of their belief in me
phrases.text: A blessing stated plainly, with belief as its ground. Verse 7 repeats the reason and sets it against the unbelief of Israel.

phrases.term: I will bring the fulness of my gospel from among them
phrases.text: The blessing has an end condition. Verse 10 lists what would bring it about.

phrases.term: They shall be numbered among my people, O house of Israel
phrases.text: Repentance makes the Gentiles part of the house. The wording matches verse 3, where the other sheep are numbered among his sheep.

phrases.term: As salt that hath lost its savor
phrases.text: The image from the sermon returns as a verdict. 3 Nephi 12:13 had used it as a warning to the multitude.
The land grant repeated. 3 Nephi 15:13 had already said the Father gave it to them.

verses.label: v. 1–3
verses.title: A category opened for the second time in two chapters
verses.text: The record used the phrase other sheep one chapter earlier, at 3 Ne. 15:21, to identify the people standing in front of the speaker. Here the same phrase is applied to a third group and the exclusions are listed: "I have other sheep, which are not of this land, neither of the land of Jerusalem, neither in any parts of that land round about whither I have been to minister." Verse 2 states what makes them a separate case, "they who have not as yet heard my voice; neither have I at any time manifested myself unto them." A term that was just given a definite reference is reopened.

verses.label: v. 10
verses.title: A charge sheet of eight items, and one clause repeated
verses.text: The record itemises the offence: "filled with all manner of lyings, and of deceits, and of mischiefs, and all manner of hypocrisy, and murders, and priestcrafts, and whoredoms, and of secret abominations." The verse also states the decisive condition twice, once at the head of the list and once after it, "shall reject the fulness of my gospel" and then "if they shall do all those things, and shall reject the fulness of my gospel." The repetition marks which item on the list actually triggers the consequence.

verses.label: v. 12–15
verses.title: Both outcomes stated, with the same conditional
verses.text: The record gives the two branches in full rather than naming only the good one. If they repent, "they shall be numbered among my people, O house of Israel," and Israel will not "tread them down." If not, verse 15 states what follows without softening: "I will suffer my people, O house of Israel, that they shall go through among them, and shall tread them down." The same population is the subject of both futures, and the pivot between them is stated in three words, "if they will not turn."

verses.label: v. 16
verses.title: A land grant reported as an order received
verses.text: The verse gives the deed and its authority in one sentence: "thus hath the Father commanded me, that I should give unto this people this land for their inheritance." The speaker is reporting an instruction rather than making a grant on his own account, which is the same construction the chapter uses at verses 3 and 10, "I have received a commandment of the Father" and "thus commandeth the Father that I should say unto you." Three times in sixteen verses the record marks the speaker as relaying rather than originating.

chapter.title: The map keeps widening
chapter.text: 3 Nephi 15 identified these hearers as the other sheep, and verse 1 immediately names a group beyond them. Each answer opens another distance.

chapter.title: He tells them what he has not done yet
chapter.text: Verse 2 says these others have never heard his voice. The chapter is willing to leave a ministry unfinished in front of the twelve.

chapter.title: The record knows its readers
chapter.text: Verse 4 names the Gentiles as the ones the writing reaches, and the remnant of this people as the ones it is for. The book states its own delivery route.

chapter.title: Blessing and warning attach to the same people
chapter.text: Verse 6 blesses the Gentiles and verse 8 pronounces a woe on the unbelieving among them. Both stand in the same speech.

chapter.title: Israel's suffering is placed under the Father's judgment
chapter.text: Verse 9 says he caused it. The chapter does not leave the scattering to accident.

chapter.title: The turn is conditional both ways
chapter.text: Verse 13 opens the house to Gentiles who repent and verse 15 hands them over if they will not. The condition is the same for everyone in the sentence.

chapter.title: A sermon image comes back as a sentence of judgment
chapter.text: 3 Nephi 12:13 gave salt as a warning to the multitude. Verse 15 applies it to nations.

chapter.title: Isaiah closes the chapter
chapter.text: Verses 18 to 20 quote Isaiah 52:8-10. The chapter ends in someone else's words about Zion coming back.

applications.title: Say plainly what you have not done
applications.text: He tells the twelve about other sheep "not of this land, neither of the land of Jerusalem," and then says he has a commandment to go to them. Naming the part of the work still outstanding, in front of people who thought they were the whole of it, is a discipline worth copying.

applications.title: Write for the reader you will never meet
applications.text: The command to write is given so that a future people can receive it "through the Holy Ghost." Some of what you are asked to do is only useful to somebody not yet born, and the temptation is to measure it by the response you get now.

applications.title: Hold the blessing and the warning together
applications.text: He blesses the Gentiles for their belief at verse 6 and pronounces a woe on their unbelief at verse 10, in the same speech and about the same group. When you describe a people, including your own, keep both halves in one paragraph.

applications.title: Notice which side of the sentence you are on
applications.text: The truth comes to the Gentiles "because of their belief in me... and because of the unbelief of you, O house of Israel." One clause is a credit and the other a debit, and both are causes of the same event. Read the sentence you are inside carefully enough to find which clause is yours.

applications.title: Leave the door open on a condition
applications.text: Gentiles who repent are numbered with the covenant people, and the terms are stated rather than implied. When you set a boundary, state the way back through it in the same breath.

applications.title: Expect the conditional to run both ways
applications.text: If they will not turn, the consequence is spelled out with the same plainness as the promise. A condition that only ever gets described on its favourable side is not being taken seriously by the person describing it.

applications.title: Hold the land as a trust
applications.text: The grant is quoted with its source attached, "thus hath the Father commanded me—that I should give unto this people this land for their inheritance." What you hold on those terms is held differently from what you hold by right.

questions.text: Who have I not yet spoken to that I intend to?
What am I writing down that is meant for later?
What have I been given because of belief and not merit?
Where have I read judgment as accident?
Which of the sins in this list is the one I keep near?
What repentance is standing between me and being numbered?
What have I seen made bare that I did not expect to see?
